paras: The killing of a Black man on the Arch Street Pike was a homicide near Little Rock, Arkansas, in early 1919, in which an unnamed "Colored man" was killed and three white men were charged with murder. The Cleveland Advocate reported the case on its front page as the arrest of a white man for the death of a "Race Man."

According to a Little Rock dispatch dated March 3, 1919, the man was killed on the Arch street pike in Pulaski County "several weeks" earlier. The dispatch did not name him or describe how or why he was killed.

Two "young white boys," Jim Kennedy and Ollie Plant, were arrested on a murder charge the day after the killing and were still in jail in early March. The Pulaski County grand jury later returned an indictment charging Quinn C. Farabee with murder in connection with the killing, and he was arrested on a Wednesday afternoon shortly before March 3. No report of a trial or its outcome was found in the coverage.

The only report found ran in the Cleveland Advocate on March 8, 1919, as a short item on page one. Its headline, "White Man Arrested For Death of Race Man," put the race of the accused and the dead man at the front, while the text itself reported the arrests and indictment without comment. The item used the paper's terms "Colored man" and "Race Man" for the victim and gave no detail beyond the legal proceedings.
